# 6.1 Polynomial hashing

Phase 6 (Strings), target rating 1900–2200. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Equal substrings in O(1) (`substring-compare`)

Compare any two substrings by their hashes after O(n) preparation.

**Works because:** Polynomial hashes of prefixes give any substring's hash; collisions are rare with a large random base and modulus.

### Hashing plus searching over length (`hash-length-search`)

Longest common prefix of two suffixes, or the longest substring appearing twice, by searching over the length.

**Works because:** "A match of length L exists" is monotone in L, and each check is a hash comparison.

### Palindromes by hashing (`palindrome-hash`)

Test whether substrings are palindromes by comparing forward and reverse hashes.

**Works because:** A substring is a palindrome exactly when it equals its reverse.

### Counting distinct substrings of a length (`distinct-by-hash`)

Count or compare distinct substrings of a fixed length by storing their hashes.

**Works because:** Equal substrings have equal hashes, and collisions are rare enough to ignore with good parameters.
